meta.title: A mechanical friend for children 孩子的机器人朋友【次】

blocks.bodyHtml:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

A mechanical friend for children

A

The development of robots that interact socially with people and assist them in everyday life has been an elusive goal of modern science. Despite impressive advances in the mechanical aspects of this problem, producing robots that bond and socialize with people for sustained periods of time has proven difficult. The most successful robots so far have been storytellers, but they have only been able to maintain human interest for a limited time and typically rely on the robot telling stories that change over time. In practice, commercially available robots seldom cross the 10-hour barrier (i.e., individual users tend to spend less than a combined total of 10 hours with the robots before losing interest). This observation is in sharp contrast to the long-term interactions and bonding that commonly develop between humans and their pets.

B

In a recent study, researchers from the Institute for Neural Computation in California introduced a state-of-the-art social robot into a classroom of 18-to-24-month-olds for five months as a way of studying human/robot interactions. The researchers, including Fumihide Tanaka and Javier R. Movellan, introduced a toddler-sized humanoid robot into a classroom at a childhood education center. One of the QRIO series of robots, the 58 cm machine, was originally developed by Sony. ‘Children of toddler age were chosen because they have no preconceived notions of robots,’ according to Tanaka. One of the goals of the study was to establish whether it was possible for social robots to maintain the interest of children beyond the 10-hour barrier.

C

The researchers sent instructions to the robot about every two minutes to do things like giggle, dance, sit down, fall down, or walk in a certain direction. The 45 sessions were videotaped, and interactions between toddlers and the robot were later analyzed. The results showed that the quality of those interactions improved steadily over 27 sessions. The interactions deteriorated quickly over the next 15 sessions, when the robot was ordered to behave in a more limited, predictable manner. Finally, the human/robot relations improved in the last three sessions, after the robot had been instructed to display its full range of behaviors.

D

‘Initially, the children treated the robot very differently from the way they treated each other,’ Tanaka said. ‘Early in the study, some children cried when QRIO fell. But a month into the study, the toddlers helped QRIO stand up by pushing its back or pulling its hands.’ ‘The most important aspect of interaction was touch,’ Tanaka said. ‘At first, the toddlers would touch the robot on its face, but later on they would touch it only on its hands and arms, like they would with other humans. Another robot-like toy named Robby, which resembled QRIO but did not move, was used as a control in the study. While hugging of QRIO increased, hugging of Robby decreased throughout the study. Furthermore, when QRIO laid down on the floor, caretaking behaviors were frequently observed toward QRIO but seldom toward Robby.’

E

The study concluded that after 45 days of immersion in a childcare center over a period of five months, long-term bonding and socialization occurred between toddlers and a state-of-the-art social robot. Overall, the interaction between children and the robot improved over time and the children progressively treated it more as a peer than a plaything. ‘To my knowledge, this is the first long-term study of this sort,’ said Ronald Arkin, a roboticist at the Georgia Institute of Technology in the US.

F

Tanaka and Movellan are now developing autonomous robots for the toddler classroom. ‘It could have great potential in educational settings, assisting teachers and enriching the classroom environment,’ Tanaka said. The researchers hope that more advanced versions of robots like QRIO could become personalized tutors to assist teachers in classrooms. A robotic tutor could react on the spot to social cues and approximate social skills like facial expression and eye gaze, they said. ‘It is becoming clear that, to achieve this goal, we are going to endow machines with something similar to emotion, not just traditional forms of intelligence,’ said Movellan.

G

Associate Professor David Powers, an expert in artificial intelligence and cognitive science at Flinders University in South Australia, commented, ‘In this study, it is clearly demonstrated that a limited range of robot behaviors, however impressive, is nowhere near as important to human/robot interaction as being able to make appropriate responses from a broad repertoire of behaviors.’ Ronald Arkin was not surprised by the affection demonstrated by the toddlers toward the robot. ‘Humans have a tremendous propensity to bond with artifacts, whether it be a car, a doll, or a robot,’ he said. But he also cautioned that researchers do not yet understand the consequences of increased human/robot interaction. ‘Studying how robots and humans work together can give us insight into whether this is a good thing or a bad thing for society,’ Arkin said. ‘We need to find out what the consequences are of introducing a robot into a cadre of children. How will that enhance, or potentially interfere with, their social development? Do we really understand the long-term impact of having a robot as a childhood friend?’

meta.title: A mechanical friend for children 孩子的机器人朋友【次】

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 开发能够与人进行社交互动并在日常生活中协助他们的机器人，一直是现代科学难以实现的目标。尽管在这一问题的机械方面取得了令人印象深刻的进展，但事实证明，制造能够与人长期建立联系和社交的机器人是困难的。迄今为止最成功的机器人是讲故事的机器人，但它们只能在有限的时间内维持人类的兴趣，而且通常依赖机器人讲述随时间变化的故事。实际上，商业可用的机器人很少能突破10小时的障碍（即，单个用户在失去兴趣之前与机器人共度的时间总计往往不到10小时）。这一观察结果与人类与宠物之间通常形成的长期互动和情感纽带形成了鲜明对比。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 在最近的一项研究中，加州神经计算研究所的研究人员将一台最先进的社交机器人引入一个18至24个月大的幼儿课堂，为期五个月，以研究人与机器人的互动。研究人员包括田中英英和哈维尔·R·莫维兰，他们将一台幼儿大小的人形机器人引入了一家儿童教育中心的教室。这台58厘米高的机器人是QRIO系列机器人之一，最初由索尼开发。田中说：“选择幼儿年龄段是因为他们对机器人没有先入为主的观念。”该研究的目标之一是确定社交机器人是否能够维持儿童的兴趣超过10小时的障碍。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 研究人员大约每两分钟向机器人发送指令，让它做诸如咯咯笑、跳舞、坐下、摔倒或向某个方向行走等动作。45次会议被录像，随后分析了幼儿与机器人之间的互动。结果表明，这些互动的质量在27次会议中稳步提高。在接下来的15次会议中，当机器人被命令以更有限、更可预测的方式行动时，互动迅速恶化。最后，在机器人被指示展示其全部行为范围后，人与机器人的关系在最后三次会议中有所改善。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 田中说：“最初，孩子们对待机器人的方式与他们彼此之间的方式非常不同。”“在研究初期，一些孩子在QRIO摔倒时会哭。但研究进行一个月后，幼儿会通过推它的背或拉它的手来帮助QRIO站起来。”田中说：“互动最重要的方面是触摸。”最初，幼儿会触摸机器人的脸，但后来他们只触摸它的手和手臂，就像对待其他人类一样。另一个名为Robby的类似机器人的玩具，外观与QRIO相似但不能移动，在研究中被用作对照组。在整个研究过程中，拥抱QRIO的次数增加，而拥抱Robby的次数减少。此外，当QRIO躺在地板上时，经常观察到对照顾QRIO的行为，但对照顾Robby的行为却很少见。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 该研究得出结论，在五个月的时间里，经过45天的沉浸在一个儿童护理中心后，幼儿与最先进的社交机器人之间出现了长期的情感纽带和社交化。总体而言，儿童与机器人之间的互动随着时间的推移而改善，孩子们逐渐更多地将其视为同伴而非玩具。美国佐治亚理工学院的机器人专家罗纳德·阿金说：“据我所知，这是此类研究中的第一项长期研究。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 田中和莫维兰现在正在为幼儿教室开发自主机器人。田中说：“它在教育环境中可能具有巨大潜力，可以辅助教师并丰富课堂环境。”研究人员希望像QRIO这样更先进的机器人版本能够成为个性化辅导教师，在课堂上辅助教师。他们说，机器人辅导教师可以即时对社交线索做出反应，并模拟面部表情和眼神注视等社交技能。莫维兰说：“越来越清楚的是，为了实现这一目标，我们将赋予机器类似于情感的东西，而不仅仅是传统形式的智能。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 南澳大利亚弗林德斯大学人工智能和认知科学专家大卫·鲍尔斯副教授评论说：“在这项研究中，清楚地证明了有限范围的机器人行为，无论多么令人印象深刻，对于人与机器人的互动来说，远不如能够从广泛的行为库中做出适当的反应重要。”罗纳德·阿金对幼儿对机器人表现出的喜爱并不感到惊讶。“人类有与物品建立联系的巨大倾向，无论是汽车、娃娃还是机器人，”他说。但他也警告说，研究人员尚不了解人与机器人互动增加的后果。“研究机器人和人类如何合作可以让我们深入了解这对社会是好事还是坏事，”阿金说。“我们需要弄清楚将机器人引入一群孩子的后果是什么。这将如何增强，或者可能干扰他们的社交发展？我们真的了解拥有一个机器人作为童年朋友的长期影响吗？”

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a comparison of children’s reactions towards different robots
题目翻译：比较孩子对不同机器人的反应。
答案：d
定位：正文 D 段，末3句
原文：While hugging of QRIO increased, hugging of Robby decreased throughout the study. Furthermore, when QRIO lay down on the floor, caretaking behaviors were frequently observed toward QRIO but seldom toward Robby.
译文：在研究期间，孩子拥抱 QRIO 的行为增加，而拥抱 Robby 的行为减少；当 QRIO 躺在地上时，孩子经常对它表现出照料行为，但几乎不会这样对待 Robby。

解析：D 段把孩子对 QRIO 与 Robby 的拥抱和照料反应直接作对比，因此选 D。

（2）题目 15：a speculation about ways robots may be able to communicate
题目翻译：推测机器人未来可能采用哪些交流方式。
答案：f
定位：正文 F 段，第3至5句
原文：The researchers hope that more advanced versions of robots like QRIO could become personalized tutors to assist teachers in classrooms. A robotic tutor could react on the spot to social cues and approximate social skills like facial expression and eye gaze, they said.
译文：研究者希望更先进的 QRIO 类机器人能成为个性化导师；机器人导师可以即时回应社会线索，并模拟面部表情和眼神等社交技能。

解析：hope、could 以及 facial expression、eye gaze 都是在展望机器人可能采用的社交沟通方式，因此选 F。

（3）题目 16：a description of changes in the way the children physically handled a robot
题目翻译：描述孩子身体接触机器人的方式发生了怎样的变化。
答案：d
定位：正文 D 段，第5句
原文：At first, the toddlers would touch the robot on its face, but later on they would touch it only on its hands and arms, like they would with other humans.
译文：起初幼儿会触摸机器人的脸，后来他们只触摸它的手和手臂，就像接触其他人一样。

解析：At first 与 later on 明确呈现从摸脸到只摸手和手臂的身体接触变化，因此选 D。

（4）题目 17：a comparison between people’s connections with animals and their connections with robots
题目翻译：比较人与动物之间的联系和人与机器人之间的联系。
答案：a
定位：正文 A 段，末2句
原文：In practice, commercially available robots seldom cross the 10-hour barrier (i.e., individual users tend to spend less than a combined total of 10 hours with the robots before losing interest). This observation is in sharp contrast to the long-term interactions and bonding that commonly develop between humans and their pets.
译文：商业机器人很少突破十小时的兴趣门槛；这与人与宠物之间通常会形成的长期互动和情感联系形成鲜明对比。

解析：in sharp contrast 明确比较了人与机器人短暂的互动和人与宠物长期的联系，因此选 A。

（5）题目 18：an account of the way one robot was programmed
题目翻译：说明某个机器人是如何被编程或控制的。
答案：c
定位：正文 C 段，第1句及末2句
原文：The researchers sent instructions to the robot about every two minutes to do things like giggle, dance, sit down, fall down, or walk in a certain direction.
译文：研究人员大约每两分钟向机器人发送一次指令，让它咯咯笑、跳舞、坐下、跌倒或朝某个方向行走。

解析：本段具体说明研究者发送指令的频率和机器人被要求执行的动作，正是其控制方式，因此选 C。

items.text:
（1）题目 19：In future, robots will not only have to think, but also to show feelings.
题目翻译：未来机器人不仅需要思考，还需要表现出情感。
答案：b
定位：正文 F 段，末句
原文：‘It is becoming clear that, to achieve this goal, we are going to endow machines with something similar to emotion, not just traditional forms of intelligence,’ said Movellan.
译文：Movellan 说：“越来越清楚的是，为实现这一目标，我们需要赋予机器类似情感的东西，而不只是传统形式的智能。”

解析：not just intelligence 与 something similar to emotion 对应题干“不仅思考，还要有情感”；说话者是 Movellan，因此选 B。

（2）题目 20：It is uncertain whether more contact between people and robots will be beneficial.
题目翻译：人与机器人增加接触是否有益，目前尚不确定。
答案：c
定位：正文 G 段，第4至6句
原文：But he also cautioned that researchers do not yet understand the consequences of increased human/robot interaction. ‘Studying how robots and humans work together can give us insight into whether this is a good thing or a bad thing for society,’ Arkin said.
译文：但他也警告说，研究人员尚不了解人机互动增加的后果。Arkin 表示，研究人和机器人如何协作，可以帮助判断这对社会究竟是好事还是坏事。

解析：do not yet understand 与 whether ... good or bad 说明利弊尚不确定；观点归于 Ronald Arkin，因此选 C。

（3）题目 21：Very young children have not yet developed ideas about robots.
题目翻译：年龄很小的孩子还没有形成关于机器人的既定观念。
答案：a
定位：正文 B 段，第4句
原文：‘Children of toddler age were chosen because they have no preconceived notions of robots,’ according to Tanaka.
译文：Tanaka 说，选择幼儿是因为他们对机器人没有先入为主的观念。

解析：have no preconceived notions 与题干“尚未形成观念”同义；该说明来自 Tanaka，因此选 A。

（4）题目 22：Robots need to perform a wide variety of actions for people to relate to them.
题目翻译：机器人需要做出多种多样的行为，人们才能与它们建立联系。
答案：d
定位：正文 G 段，第1句
原文：Associate Professor David Powers, an expert in artificial intelligence and cognitive science at Flinders University in South Australia, commented, ‘In this study, it is clearly demonstrated that a limited range of robot behaviors, however impressive, is nowhere near as important to human/robot interaction as being able to make appropriate responses from a broad repertoire of behaviors.’
译文：David Powers 指出，有限的机器人行为范围无论多么令人印象深刻，都远不如从广泛的行为库中作出恰当回应对人机互动重要。

解析：a broad repertoire of behaviors 对应 wide variety of actions；观点由 David Powers 提出，因此选 D。

（5）题目 23：Using robots as an aid in schools may have many benefits.
题目翻译：在学校把机器人用作辅助工具可能有许多好处。
答案：a
定位：正文 F 段，第2句
原文：‘It could have great potential in educational settings, assisting teachers and enriching the classroom environment,’ Tanaka said.
译文：Tanaka 说：“它在教育环境中可能具有巨大潜力，可以协助教师并丰富课堂环境。”

解析：great potential、assisting teachers 和 enriching the classroom environment 对应“在学校使用有许多好处”；说话者是 Tanaka，因此选 A。

定位：正文 G 段，第4至6句
原文：But he also cautioned that researchers do not yet understand the consequences of increased human/robot interaction. ‘Studying how robots and humans work together can give us insight into whether this is a good thing or a bad thing for society,’ Arkin said.
译文：但他也警告说，研究人员尚不了解人机互动增加的后果。Arkin 表示，研究人和机器人如何协作，可以帮助判断这对社会究竟是好事还是坏事。

解析：do not yet understand 与 whether ... good or bad 说明利弊尚不确定；观点归于 Ronald Arkin，因此选 C。

（3）题目 21：Very young children have not yet developed ideas about robots.
题目翻译：年龄很小的孩子还没有形成关于机器人的既定观念。
答案：a
定位：正文 B 段，第4句
原文：‘Children of toddler age were chosen because they have no preconceived notions of robots,’ according to Tanaka.
译文：Tanaka 说，选择幼儿是因为他们对机器人没有先入为主的观念。

解析：have no preconceived notions 与题干“尚未形成观念”同义；该说明来自 Tanaka，因此选 A。

（4）题目 22：Robots need to perform a wide variety of actions for people to relate to them.
题目翻译：机器人需要做出多种多样的行为，人们才能与它们建立联系。
答案：d
定位：正文 G 段，第1句
原文：Associate Professor David Powers, an expert in artificial intelligence and cognitive science at Flinders University in South Australia, commented, ‘In this study, it is clearly demonstrated that a limited range of robot behaviors, however impressive, is nowhere near as important to human/robot interaction as being able to make appropriate responses from a broad repertoire of behaviors.’
译文：David Powers 指出，有限的机器人行为范围无论多么令人印象深刻，都远不如从广泛的行为库中作出恰当回应对人机互动重要。

解析：a broad repertoire of behaviors 对应 wide variety of actions；观点由 David Powers 提出，因此选 D。

（5）题目 23：Using robots as an aid in schools may have many benefits.
题目翻译：在学校把机器人用作辅助工具可能有许多好处。
答案：a
定位：正文 F 段，第2句
原文：‘It could have great potential in educational settings, assisting teachers and enriching the classroom environment,’ Tanaka said.
译文：Tanaka 说：“它在教育环境中可能具有巨大潜力，可以协助教师并丰富课堂环境。”

解析：great potential、assisting teachers 和 enriching the classroom environment 对应“在学校使用有许多好处”；说话者是 Tanaka，因此选 A。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Until recently, robots that were best at holding people’s attention were those that acted as ________.
题目翻译：直到最近，最擅长吸引人们注意力的机器人都是扮演________的机器人。
答案：storytellers
定位：正文 A 段，第3句
原文：The most successful robots so far have been storytellers, but they have only been able to maintain human interest for a limited time and typically rely on the robot telling stories that change over time.
译文：到目前为止，最成功的机器人一直是讲故事者，但它们只能在有限时间内维持人的兴趣，通常依靠机器人讲述会随时间变化的故事。

解析：题干 acted as 改写 have been；robots 为复数，原文相应表语是 storytellers，因此填 storytellers。

（2）题目 25：The children responded to the QRIO robot as a friend or a ________ rather than as a toy.
题目翻译：孩子把 QRIO 当作朋友或________，而不是玩具。
答案：peer
定位：正文 E 段，第2句
原文：Overall, the interaction between children and the robot improved over time and the children progressively treated it more as a peer than a plaything.
译文：总体而言，孩子与机器人的互动随时间改善，孩子逐渐更多地把它当作同伴，而不是玩物。

解析：as a peer than a plaything 对应题干 as a ... rather than as a toy；空格应填 peer。

（3）题目 26：Arkin expected that the children would show ________ towards the QRIO robot.
题目翻译：Arkin 预料孩子会对 QRIO 机器人表现出________。
答案：affection
定位：正文 G 段，第2句
原文：Ronald Arkin was not surprised by the affection demonstrated by the toddlers toward the robot.
译文：Ronald Arkin 对幼儿向机器人表现出的喜爱并不感到惊讶。

解析：not surprised 表明这种反应符合他的预期；affection demonstrated ... toward 改写为 show affection towards，因此填 affection。caretaking 不属于 Arkin 的预期表述，propensity 表示倾向而非孩子表现出的情感。
